news.title: U-17: Enabulele Hails Flamingos’ Historic World Cup Triumph, Celebrates Nigeria’s Golden Generation
news.lede: The Executive Chairman of the Edo State Sports Commission, Hon. Amadin Desmond Enabulele, has congratulated Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, on their historic 2-1 victory over Japan to emerge champions of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat, Morocco. In a statement issued by his Media Aide, Edoko Wilson Edoko, Enabulele described the triumph as a remarkable demonstration of courage, resilience, determination and the Nigerian fighting spirit, noting that the young footballers had etched their names in history by becoming the first Nigerian team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.

news.title: Flamingos Rewarded After Historic FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup Triumph
news.lede: Nigeria's national U-17 women's football team, known as the Flamingos, secured a historic victory by defeating Japan 2-1 in the final match of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup. This triumph marked the first time an African team has claimed this global title, elevating Nigeria to become the sole African nation to win the FIFA U-17 World Cup in both the men's and women's categories. The victory was celebrated with a special reception hosted in Rabat, Morocco, on Saturday night, honoring the players and officials for their remarkable achievement on the international stage. Reception Details and Immediate RewardsShehu Dikko, the Chairman of the National Sports Commission, and Bukola Olopade, the Director General, organized a formal reception to celebrate the team's success.

news.title: FULL LIST: 20 youngest FIFA World Cup winners
news.lede: Barcelona and Spain winger, Lamine Yamal posing with the World Cup after beating Argentina in 2026 Photo: FIFA. Winning the FIFA World Cup is one of the greatest achievements in football, but doing so before turning 21 is a remarkable feat that places a player among an exclusive group of young champions. Brazilian legend Pelé tops the list of the 20 youngest players to win the FIFA World Cup, having achieved the historic milestone at just 17 years and 249 days during the 1958 tournament in Sweden. Pelé remains the youngest player ever to become a World Cup champion.

news.title: Nigeria wins FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup for the first time, stuns Japan in final
news.lede: Chennai Awawu Bashiru came to the fore once again as Nigeria beat Japan 2-1 to win its first-ever FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup title in Rabat, Morocco, on Saturday. Bashiru, who had netted a brace against Brazil in the semifinal, opened the scoring in the 39th minute, converting from a pass by Mary Dunstan.
